A Randomized Phase 3 Study Comparing P2B001 to its Components (Low-Dose 
Extended-Release Rasagiline and Pramipexole) and to Optimized Doses of Marketed 
Extended-Release Pramipexole in Early Parkinson's Disease.

Olanow CW(1)(2), Hauser RA(3), Burdick DJ(4), Dhall R(5), de Marcaida JA(6), Gil

Study Group.

(10)Cooper Medical School of Rowan University, Camden, New Jersey, USA.
(11)Center for Health and Technology, University of Rochester, Rochester, New 
York, USA.

BACKGROUND: There remains uncertainty as to the optimal way to initiate therapy 
for Parkinson's disease (PD) to maximize benefit and minimize adversity.
OBJECTIVES: The objective was to determine if P2B001 (a fixed, low-dose, 
extended-release [ER] combination of pramipexole 0.6 mg and rasagiline 0.75 mg) 
is superior to each of its components and compare its safety and efficacy to 
optimized treatment with marketed doses of pramipexole-ER.
